newsitem.title: USA: Rising tide lifts U.S. offshore drilling companies.
newsitem.headline: Rising tide lifts U.S. offshore drilling companies.

text.p: Shares in offshore drilling companies rose Tuesday as investor sentiment shifted on prospects of steady to higher oil prices on the horizon, company executives said.

Offshore drilling stocks have been moving in tandem with oil price projections in recent weeks, and executives said the tide shifted again today on a bullish Wall Street Journal article which forecast an end to this year's falling prices.
"I think the market overcorrected over the last several days," Global Marine Inc Vice President David Herasimchuk said of a recent drop in the sector's stock prices.

In a conference call Monday, Global Marine executives reminded analysts of their outlook that offshore services firms benefit more from moderate oil prices than from boom-and-bust cycles that can follow a sharp run-up in prices, he said.
A spokeswoman with Diamond Offshore said the company has been talking with analysts interested in initiating coverage but could not account for active trading in its shares on the day.
"There's nothing fundamental about our buisiness that has changed," said spokeswoman Karen Steffes.
Global Marine was up 2-1/8 at 19-7/8, Transocean Offshore was up 4 at 58-1/4 and Diamond Offshore was up 5-1/2 at 60-7/8 on heavy volume in late-afternoon New York Stock Exchange trading.
